title: MDP2 Forest: A Constrained Continuous Multi-dimensional Policy Optimization Approach for Short-video Recommendation

problem.claim: Short-video platforms need to determine the optimal exposure proportion of each video category to guide recommendation systems and content production.

gap.claim: Existing recommendation studies focus on matching videos to view requests but may produce serious issues when selection bias and exposure bias are not considered.

contributions.claim: The paper formalizes exposure proportion strategy as a constrained policy-making problem with multi-dimensional continuous treatment from a causal inference perspective.
The paper proposes MDP2 Forest, an ensemble policy learning method based on causal trees for constrained multi-dimensional policy optimization.
MDP2 Forest is described as adaptable to business settings involving different kinds of constraints on multi-dimensional treatment.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe MDP2 Forest as a novel ensemble policy learning method based on causal trees.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on simulated and synthetic datasets report superiority over other policy learning or causal inference methods in treatment estimation accuracy and mean regret.

narrative_sequence.summary: Category-level exposure proportions are important for guiding short-video recommendation and content production.
Matching videos to requests without accounting for selection and exposure bias can create serious issues.
The exposure strategy is formulated as a constrained policy-making problem with multi-dimensional continuous treatment.
The authors introduce the causal-tree-based MDP2 Forest ensemble policy learning method.
Reported experiments compare the method on simulated and synthetic datasets, and the method is described as adaptable to constrained business settings.

source_observation.claim: The paper models category exposure proportions as a constrained multi-dimensional continuous treatment policy.

interpretation.claim: Recommendation interventions can be analyzed at a policy level rather than only as individual request-level matching decisions.

application.claim: Use causal policy learning when optimizing aggregate exposure strategies under operational constraints.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which constraints, business settings, or deployment conditions are supported.

source_observation.claim: The reported evaluation uses simulated and synthetic datasets and measures treatment estimation accuracy and mean regret.

interpretation.claim: The method is evaluated on policy-learning objectives that combine treatment estimation and decision quality.

application.claim: Assess constrained policy-learning methods with both estimation-oriented and regret-oriented metrics.
